name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: Afghanistan plan 32% funded; Gaza rations cut
summary: OCHA says Afghanistan's appeal is 32% funded before winter; WFP has cut Gaza aid; no large-scale suspension found
state: OCHA said on 18 Nov that only 32% of the $1.71 billion needed for Afghanistan had been secured ahead of winter (8am Media). WFP cut Gaza food assistance in October from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people a month, and UNHCR and IOM said on 6 Nov they can prioritise shelter aid for only about 10% of those in need in Sudan, with IOM warehouses empty. Major ration cuts meet Watch; no large-scale suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country was found as of 25 Nov.
for_you: Cuts fall hardest on people relying on food, shelter and health aid in Sudan, Gaza, Afghanistan and other crises. OCHA's Financial Tracking Service publishes funding levels.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration cuts announced (WFP Gaza); no pipeline break forcing large-scale suspension

sources.title: 8am Media — OCHA: Afghanistan faces humanitarian funding shortfall ahead of winter
WFP — Funding cuts force WFP to drastically reduce lifesaving assistance in Gaza
TimesLIVE — Millions of displaced Sudanese risk losing shelter as funds run low, UN warns

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
